tours.title: How a job is dispatched and retried
tours.summary: The runner takes each job from an in-memory queue and runs it on a worker. When an attempt fails, the runner puts the job back on the queue with a growing delay. A later pass of the same loop takes the job again. This tour leaves out the inside of the worker and the metrics.

steps.note:
### Two files decide which job runs next

Scheduling is the runner and the queue. The runner decides what happens to each job, and the queue keeps the jobs and their due times.

### Each pass of the loop takes one job

The loop runs while the runner is running. Each pass asks the queue for the next due job. When no job is due, the loop waits and asks again.

### A worker runs one attempt

The runner leases a free worker and runs the job with a timeout. The worker reports a failure in its result and does not throw.

### A failed job goes back on the queue

With retries left, the runner requeues the job with a delay that doubles each time. A later `pop()` hands the job out again. With no retries left, the job goes to the dead-letter list.

### Where to go next

The worker box answers how one attempt times out. The metrics box answers how the metrics count finished jobs from events on the bus.
